module.purpose: Server-side props for the public user profile page ([user]) — handles org domain redirects, dynamic group redirects, fetches user(s) and public event types, and computes profile/entity/bio data for SEO-safe rendering.
module.summary: This Next.js getServerSideProps function powers the public profile page. It resolves the username list from the query, checks organization domain validity, and redirects to org-specific or dynamic-group URLs when needed. It fetches user records via UserRepository (with a platform-member fallback), retrieves public event types, and builds page props including user bio (markdown-safe), branding colors, entity details, and SEO indexing flags. It also supports a debug header for data-fetch time and a one-event redirect. The helper getUsersInOrgContext abstracts user lookup across org and platform contexts.
module.businessContext: For Cal.com, a scheduling platform. Public profile pages let users share booking links and showcase event types. Failures here mean broken profiles, lost bookings, and degraded SEO or organization redirect behavior.
classes: UserPageProps (~L25-75): Defines props shape for the user profile page, including profile, users, eventTypes, entity, and embed props.
functions: getServerSideProps (~L77-199): Fetches user data, handles redirects, and returns page props.
getUsersInOrgContext (~L201-220): Retrieves users by username within an org, falling back to platform members.
systemCapabilities: Fetch public user profiles and event types
Handle organization and dynamic group redirects
Provide SEO-safe bio and indexing flags
Apply branding colors from user settings
Support embed props for iframe embedding

moduleContractTests.then: result.redirect.destination starts with '/alice+bob/dynamic?' and result.redirect.permanent === false
moduleContractTests.rationale: Ensures the dynamic group redirect behavior is preserved.

moduleContractTests.rationale: Guards the 404 behavior for non-existent users outside org context.

moduleContractTests.rationale: Ensures the single-event redirect shortcut is honored.
